Madam President, One year ago, the international community gathered here for the historic conference on the implementation of the two-state solution, co-hosted by France and Saudi Arabia. The adoption of the New York Declaration, endorsed by the General Assembly by an overwhelming majority, demonstrated the breadth of international support for this objective. Last week, at the Global Alliance Ministerial Meeting for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution, the international community once again underscored that there remains only one credible path towards lasting peace and security for Palestinians and Israelis: two states living side by side in peace and security, in accordance with international law and the relevant UN resolutions. The task before us is to ensure that this political horizon does not disappear while we address the immediate challenges in Gaza. It is now time for broad international consensus to be translated into concrete action. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Greece, and I give the floor to the representative of Pakistan.

Madam President, we thank Mr. Ramiz Alakbarov acting special coordinator for his comprehensive and valuable briefing. We also take note of the poignant remarks delivered by the civil society briefers. We empathize with their pain and loss. Last week, world leaders gathered for the high level week of the General Assembly. Across the many meetings and statements, one message emerged with unmistakable clarity. The two state solution remains the internationally agreed framework for the Palestinian question and the indispensable foundation for a just and lasting peace. Yet, this shared commitment is being undermined by deliberate actions by Israel, the occupying power, to create irreversible facts on the ground. In the occupied West Bank, including the East Jerusalem, illegal settlement expansion is being pursued as a deliberate strategy to alter the demographic and geographic character of Palestinian territory. The rapid advancement of the E1 project, with tenders for 3,401 housing units, threatens to sever territorial contiguity and undermine the possibility of a viable Palestinian state. Settler violence has escalated to alarming levels, with OCHA recording over 1,600 attacks this year alone. These are no longer isolated incidents, but organized assaults on Palestinian communities, enabled by impunity, endorsed by state apparatus. Together with demolitions, land seizures, forced displacement, and expanding Israeli administrative control, they are entrenching annexation and dismantling the foundations of peace. Madam President, we cannot affirm Palestinian statehood while allowing its territorial foundations to be destroyed. Action is required. Pakistan welcomes the sanctions measures announced by the United Kingdom, France and Canada concerning goods originating from illegal settlements, and the similar steps announced by other countries. These measures send an important message: unlawful settlement activity and those who sustain it must face consequences. Madam President, The situation in Gaza remains deeply disturbing. The approaching winter threatens to deepen an already dire humanitarian crisis, with the population confined to roughly 30% of Gaza's territory in deplorable conditions. Since the ceasefire, more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli aggression, underscoring the urgent need to ensure effective protection for the population. Diplomatic efforts have established mutually reinforcing frameworks, including Security Council Resolution 2803, the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, and the New York Declaration. Pakistan supports their full, good-faith implementation. All relevant implementation mechanisms must reinforce these shared objectives and advance a credible political horizon. The immediate requirements are clear. All settlement activities must cease. Settler violence halted. Accountability ensured. Measures advancing annexation reversed. In Gaza, Resolution 2803 must be fully implemented, including full implementation of the ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, and reconstruction. Any attempt to forcibly displace population in West Bank and Gaza or usurp its territory must be unequivocally rejected. And the Palestinian Authority must be empowered, including through the release of withheld revenues. Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, constitute a single territorial unit. We must reject any attempt to sever or fragment their territorial unity and integrity. Our collective efforts must converge on a credible, time-bound, and irreversible political process ending the Israeli occupation and establishing an independent, sovereign, and contiguous state of Palestine on the pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds al-Sharif as its capital. The Palestinian people should not have to wait. Peace might not be able to survive another cycle of promises without implementation. I thank you.
I thank the representative of Pakistan, and I give the floor to the representative of China.

Madam President, I thank Acting Special Coordinator Alec Barrow for his briefing. I also thank Mr. Inon and Mr. Apsara for sharing with us the radiance of humanity that shines through their statements. Last week, During the general debate and other high-level meetings of the 81st session of the GA, the Palestinian question was one of the focal points addressed by member states. There was a clarion call by the broad UN membership for choosing ceasefire over conflict, dialogue over hate, and a two-state solution over occupation and annexation. The urgency of the relentlessly deteriorating situation on the occupied Palestinian territories should compel the international community to build greater consensus and translate those powerful voices into practical actions in order to prevent the two-state solution from fading away and help bring about a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement to the Palestinian question at an early date. I'll make three points. First, Every effort must be made to avert a collapse in the West Bank. As the occupying power persists in relentlessly accelerating the expansion of settlements, many Palestinians have seen evictions from their homes, their livelihoods lost, families torn apart, and loved ones killed. Settlements violate Security Council Resolution 2334 and the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, and as such, have no legal validity. Any act of annexation in the West Bank, de facto or otherwise, diminishes the viability of Palestinian lives and gravely undermines the territorial foundation of Palestinian statehood. China urges Israel to immediately cease and rescind its settlement projects, stop appropriating Palestinian homes and encroaching on Palestinian territories, and take effective measures to curb settler violence and ensure strict accountability for all cases of attacks. Israel should, without delay, return withheld tax revenues, remove unreasonable economic restrictions in the West Bank, and stop undermining the foundation on which the PA exercises its governance authority. Second. Every effort must be made to improve the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Gaza is still under siege from all sides, with life-sustaining supplies running short, sewage left uncleared, and buildings reduced to rubble everywhere, in a humanitarian situation that is no longer tolerable. However, Israel continues its relentless attacks on Gaza, with each day producing new numbers of casualties. As long as bombs continue to drop and humanitarian access remains obstructed in Gaza, peace will not be able to take shape, nor will reconstruction get off the ground. We call on the relevant parties, Israel in particular, to sincerely and fully implement ceasefire obligations, immediately cease all military operations in Gaza, and take positive steps towards lasting peace. Israel must fulfill its obligations under international humanitarian law by lifting restrictions on humanitarian access to allow shelter and requisite equipment to enter Gaza, and stop restricting and attacking UNRWA and other humanitarian organizations. Third, Every effort must be made to implement a two-state solution. The situation between Palestine and Israel before us today is fundamentally a result of Palestinians' right to statehood, right to life, and right of return being ignored for far too long. The ultimate way to break the cycle of conflicts between Palestine and Israel is to implement the two-state solution, restore the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, and establish an independent Palestinian state. The international community must rally greater efforts to take irreversible actions and to revitalize the prospect of the two-state solution. We should all reject any attempt to alter the Palestinian territories and their demographic structures, and oppose any unilateral action to undermine the foundation of the two-state solution. We call for upholding the principle of Palestinians governing Palestine in advancing the governance of West Bank and the post-war reconstruction of Gaza. Any effort taken by the international community on the Palestinian question should help, not harm, the two-state solution. President, the general debate of this UNGA session is drawing to a close, but the international community should not break step in working for a settlement of the Palestinian question. China stands consistently on the side of peace, justice, and the conscience of humanity. and stands ready, as always, to make greater efforts for a political settlement of the Palestinian question and for lasting peace and stability in the Middle East. I thank you, President.
I thank the representative of China for that statement. I now give the floor to the representative of the United Kingdom.

I thank Acting Special Coordinator Al-Agbarov for his briefing, and I also thank Mr. Inon and Mr. Abu Sara for their powerful testimonies. and the compelling call for a future based on peaceful coexistence. Throughout high-level week, we heard a clear and repeated commitment to achieving a two-state solution. It remains the only credible path forward to a better future for Israelis and Palestinians, founded on lasting peace and security for both. Yet the two-state solution is at risk of being destroyed by the facts on the ground. Mr. President, My Prime Minister has been clear. The 7 October 2023 terrorist attack on Israel was monstrous, and he has condemned Hamas' actions in the strongest terms. The United Kingdom continues to stand with Israel in the face of ongoing threats, including from Iran. But my Prime Minister has also been clear that this does not justify the government of Israel's actions in the West Bank and Gaza. In the West Bank, Israel continues to expand settlements at pace, in violation of international law and contrary to resolution 2334. We are approaching a point of no return with the E1 settlement project. We welcome the reports that the deadline for bids may be delayed, but a temporary delay is not enough. It would sever East Jerusalem from the West Bank and endanger the viability of a two-state solution. This project must not go ahead. Alongside the rapid expansion of settlements, we have also seen an alarming increase in settler violence. The government of Israel must prevent violence in all of its forms and ensure proper accountability for perpetrators. Pardons and decisions not to bring charges against Israeli soldiers who have committed violent crimes sends the opposite message. The United Kingdom is acting with international partners to protect the two-state solution. Together with partners, we have announced our intention to legislate to ban the import of goods from illegal settlements and bring in sanctions against those who finance, support and facilitate illegal settlements. We have been clear that we view the Israeli occupation of Palestinian land as unlawful. We continue to support the Palestinian Authority's reform agenda and welcome its commitments to hold elections. Credible, transparent and reformed public institutions remain essential to a future Palestinian state. We welcome the recent extension by Israel of correspondent banking relationships, but we need urgent action to reverse policies which are crippling the West Bank economy. Further measures must include the release of clearance revenues to the Palestinian Authority, ensuring sustainable and predictable banking arrangements, easing movement and access restrictions, facilitating trade, and improving access to employment and economic opportunities. Turning to Gaza, the United Kingdom remains fully committed to implementation of resolution 2803 and the 20-point peace plan. Hamas must decommission its weapons, dismantle its terrorist infrastructure, and completely relinquish its control of Gaza. The United Kingdom has pledged $117 million in humanitarian early recovery assistance this year, but aid cannot save lives if it cannot reach people. With another winter approaching, urgent action is needed. Last week, my Foreign Secretary, alongside Jordan and Qatar, brought partners together behind a call to action on humanitarian access and healthcare in Gaza. The focus must now be on turning that shared commitment into tangible improvements for people on the ground. Israel must lift all restrictions on humanitarian aid, stop the gilling in Gaza, and withdraw. Mr. President, we're at a critical juncture. The peoples of Israel and Palestine deserve a better future. This Council must do all we can to protect the two-state solution, bolster stability in the West Bank, and bring the suffering in Gaza to an end.

I thank you.

I thank the representative of the United Kingdom for her statement. I would now like to make a statement in my capacity as representative of France. I would like to thank the Acting Special Coordinator, Mr. Ramiz Alkbarov, and also the representatives of civil society, Mr. Maouz Inon and Mr. Aziz Abou-Sahra, for their briefings. They talked about the developments in the worrying situation, and they confirmed that there is a path for peace, for security, and even for reconciliation. that needs to be taken. A week ago, the French president, along with his UK, Canadian and Saudi partners, brought together at the UN several states to have an exchange of views on the implementation of the two-state solution, a year after the adoption of the New York Declaration and our recognition of the State of Palestine. In its wake, the French foreign minister As you said, it brought together representatives of Israeli and Palestinian civil society who work on a daily basis to preserve the two-state solution. What emerged from these exchanges is clear. The risk that we are facing is that all of these efforts be in vain the strikes on civilians and infrastructure in Gaza continue that the strip remains in ruins and that the West Bank room is irrevocably carved up that the two-state solution disappear and that peace and Regional Security become unattainable that is the risk we cannot accept this This would entail a grim future both for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people to exist and to enjoy having a state, and also for Israel's security. And we reiterate our unfailing support for that. In the West Bank, we are seeing an Israeli policy of annexation, a flagrant violation of international law and Resolution 2334. This policy is reflected by the systemic expansion of settlements, including the E1 project, despite firm warnings. There is unbridled violence by the settlers and by the financial suffocation of the Palestinian Authority and by the soon irreversible erosion of the territorial continuity of a Palestinian state. Along with the UK and Canada, we've therefore taken additional measures to uphold our commitment to preserve the two-state solution before it's too late. We've banned the import of products from the settlements that are illegal under international law, and we have imposed targeted sanctions on those responsible for settlement activity and violence. We remain mobilized to adopt a similar ban at the European level. Preserving the two-state solution involves renewing Palestinian governance. President Abbas last year made important commitments in the area of reform that have been long-awaited. Substantial progress has been made and confirmed by independent bodies. This progress must continue. These reforms go hand in hand with the commitment to organize legislative and presidential elections soon. These are key for strengthening Palestinian governance and for renewing its legitimacy. France is ready to support this electoral process and would urge all parties to guarantee that it runs smoothly. In Gaza, we know what needs to be done. Hamas that is guilty of enormous terrorist attack needs to disarm. Israel needs to withdraw and the NCAG needs to deploy to provide for a reformed Palestinian Authority returning. A disarmament plan is on the table. We would urge Israel to take this opportunity and to make progress. The humanitarian situation remains catastrophic despite some progress. France is mobilized to meet the people's needs. We have allocated 345 million EUR in assistance since 2023 and we will continue our commitment. We will. remain committed to reconstruction efforts, in particular through the UN Horizon Fund, and we've granted 5 million to that. Israel needs to facilitate the entrance of humanitarian assistance and goods that are essential, even though they be dual use. One year after the New York Declaration, we need to reiterate that this is absolutely crucial for the Palestinians to rebuild. So the responsibility that the Council has is enormous, bringing back from the brink the two-state solution, and this is the only path forward for a lasting peace. I resume my function as President of the Council, and I give the floor to the Permanent Observer of the Observer State of Palestine. Thank you.

Mr. President, allow me at the outset to thank France for its leadership in the pursuit of just peace, including in its capacity as chair of the International Conference on the Peaceful Settlement of the Question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution together with Saudi Arabia. That leadership was evident in France's recognition of the State of Palestine and the dynamic it created with many countries joining this movement. We noticed that some expressed outrage for a mistake in the choice of words in President Macron's speech at the UN General Assembly. For the most part, they are the ones who are responsible for horrific crimes or advocates trying to distract attention away from the worldwide condemnation of Israel's actions. The New York Declaration embodies a clear vision for a future of freedom, justice, peace, and shared security and prosperity in the Middle East for all states and all peoples. It is those obstructing that horizon that are cause for outrage and that must be held accountable. Allow me also to thank Acting Special Coordinator Alakbarov for presenting the Secretary-General's report pursuant to Resolution 2334, which reflects the existential threat faced by the Palestinian people. Allow me, Mr. President, also to thank Aziz and Moaz for their testimonies and for their struggle for shared humanity and peace. The way they have transformed their loss into a call for blind vengeance, but for true justice and peace is an inspiration for all of us all. I thank you very much for being with us, and we salute your courage and commitment to humanity and peace. You are the great example that should inspire everyone for action, especially the Security Council. Mr. President, at this high-level week, comes to an end, as this high-level week comes to an end, the voice that was supposed to be silenced resonated everywhere. Palestine was everywhere. It was the biggest elephant in the UN building and maybe through the city of New York. An attempt was made to exclude Palestine, yet Palestine was heard. 152 states voted to ensure it, rejecting the denial of visas for the Palestinian delegation in violation of the obligations of the host country and ensuring its participation on equal footing with other states. The Palestinian people were seen and their rights reaffirmed by so many leaders from across the globe. And the Israeli prime minister who was able to attend, despite being subject to an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, faced a walkout, and his government's policies faced rejection from countries across the world. Palestine remains a North Star for all those who believe in humanity. freedom, international law, and justice. Mr. President, nearly 10 years have passed since this Council adopted resolution 2334. Its provisions could not be clearer. It reaffirms the inadmissibility of the acquisition of land by force. It condemns all measures aimed at altering the demographic composition, character, and status of the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem. It reaffirms that Israeli settlements have no legal validity and constitute a flagrant violation under international law. It demands an end to all settlement activities. It reminds states of their obligations in this regard. Yet, report after report, we are confronted with developments moving in precisely the opposite direction. Settlements expand. Palestinian land is confiscated. Homes are demolished. communities are forcibly displaced, settler terror continues, and measures of annexations accelerate. We must be clear. Annexation is not simply a future threat. It is being advanced on the ground, piece by piece, through violence, settlements, infrastructure, displacement, land seizures. Now, faster than ever. This is true in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and in the Gaza Strip. The E1 is a plan, is a culmination of this plan. Its aim is clear as spelled out by Israeli leaders. Kill the Palestinian state and with it, any prospect for peace. The Secretary General himself has rightly described E1 as an existential threat to the two-state solution. E1 must be stopped. I repeat, E1 must be stopped. In parallel, Israel is seeking the collapse of the PA. as that would provide a unique opportunity to push for the last stages of its plan for forcible displacement and replacement of our people and annexation of our land. Our principles must therefore remain unequivocal. Upholding the ceasefire, no occupation, No annexation. No forcible displacement. Reunification of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip under the Palestinian Authority. Fulfillment of the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination. And realization of the independence of the State of Palestine. Respect for the rights of all peoples and the sovereignty and security of all states. These are the principles enshrined in international law and reflected in the New York Declaration and the comprehensive plan, and that enjoy worldwide support. They must be implemented. While Palestine, Arab and Muslim countries, and the international community and the UN are doing their part in advancing such implementation, Israel continues not only obstructing progress, but violating the ceasefire and its obligations and commitments, including in relation to annexation. The whole world is in one direction, and Israel rebelling and rejecting the position of the whole world. Mr. President. Resolution 2334 was not adopted merely to express concern. Security Council resolutions cannot become optional, implemented by some, ignored by others, and remembered only every three months when this Council meets to document their violations. International law cannot operate according to the identity of the violator. Accountability cannot depend upon political convenience, and Palestine rights cannot remain perpetually contingent upon the occupying power's will and whims. For decades, the international community has condemned settlements, yet settlements have continued to expand. Condemnation without consequences has not produced compliance. The time has come to move from statements to measures, from condemnation to accountability, and from declarations of solidarity to implementation. This means accountability consistent with international law for those responsible for settler violence, forced displacement, and illegal settlement expansion. It means disarming settlers in line with UN Security Council Resolution 904. It means stopping E1, including by holding accountable government officials, businesses, and banks and making clear that further annexation measures will have consequences. It means protecting Palestinian civilians and communities facing displacement and violence. And it means strengthening Palestinian steadfastness and institutions through sustained political and financial support, as well as providing support for UNRWA and the wider United Nations humanitarian system. Mr. President, there is an additional legal reality this Council cannot ignore. In its advisory opinion of 19 July 2024, the International Court of Justice found that Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory is unlawful. The court also addressed the responsibilities of third states, all of you. States are under an obligation not to recognize as legal the situation arising from Israel's unlawful presence in the occupied Palestinian territory and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining that situation. That's an obligation on you. articulated by the court. They must also distinguish in their dealings between Israel and the occupied Palestinian territory. They must uphold the Geneva Conventions. Those findings must have meaning in practice. No State should assist in maintaining an illegal situation created through occupation, settlement or annexation. No commercial relationship, financial flow or other form of assistance should contribute to the perpetuation of illegal settlements. And all states must support the realization of the Palestinian people's right to self-determination. In short, no money, no trade, no arms to prolong the unlawful occupation and sanctions and measures to bring it to an end. We welcome the measures taken by states, including the United Kingdom. I was in meetings listening to the Prime Minister of the UK, President Macron, Prime Minister of Canada, Foreign Minister of Saudi Arabia, and dozens of prime ministers, vice prime ministers in celebrating the one-year anniversary of the New York Declaration. They all are supporting this courageous position of sanctions to bring Israel into compliance to its obligation and the will of the international community and international law. We welcome the measures taken by states, including the United Kingdom, as I have said, in this regard, and call for amplifying this movement that is indispensable to stop the attempt to liquidate the Palestinian question and to destroy the two-state solution. Mr. President, the Palestinian people do not need another decade of reports documenting the disappearance of their land. They need protection. They need institutions sustained. They need the ceasefire upheld, humanitarian aid to flow in Gaza. and to rebuild Gaza. They need East Jerusalem and its Muslim and Christian holy sites protected. They need settlement and annexation stopped. They need accountability. And above all, they need freedom and the realization of their inalienable right to self-determination and independence. This high-level week demonstrated that Palestine cannot be erased, cannot be ignored, cannot act as if Palestine does not exist. We are the giants in this building, in the house of peace and justice, the United Nations. Its people cannot be rendered invisible. and their rights cannot be extinguished by genocide, occupation, settlement, or annexation. So the question before us is no longer whether the international community has spoken. It has. The question is whether our words will finally have consequences. That is the difference between life and death, freedom and oppression, peace and war. That is what will determine what the future will reserve to a new generation of Palestinian and Israelis and for our region. A free Palestine is the gateway towards a peaceful Middle East. Free Palestine is the gateway for peace for all of us, including our neighbors, the Israelis. Thank you very much.
I thank the Permanent Observer of the Observer State of Palestine for that statement, and I give the floor to the representative of Israel.

Mr. President, I would like to thank Ramiz Alagbarov, Acting Special Coordinator for the Middle East, for his briefing. This month marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks here in New York. Nearly 3,000 people were killed, thousands more were injured, and many continue to suffer the consequences to this day. In the face of that horror, the international community faced a choice: remain silent or stand united against terrorism. This Council chose unity and action. Through Resolution 1373 and other measures, it strengthened the global counterterrorism framework and acted against al-Qaeda and the Taliban. The message was unequivocal. When confronted with terrorism, the international community would stand together and fight it. Mr. President, next month, the State of Israel will mark three years since Hamas's October 7th massacre. On that day, 1,200 people were murdered, thousands more were injured, and 251 men, women, children, and babies, Israelis and foreign nationals alike, were taken hostage into Gaza. Over the years, dozens of countries have formally designated Hamas as a terrorist organization. including the United States and all 27 members of the European Union. Six current members of this Council are among them. Yet three years after October 7th, the Security Council has still not designated Hamas as a terrorist organization. That is not only incomprehensible, it undermines the very message this Council should send against terrorism. Mr. President, In the past few weeks, we have seen sanctions by some countries targeting the Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria. And today, we heard many speakers talking about these Israeli communities and the so-called settler violence as the obstacle to peace. Let me be clear. Israel condemns all forms of violence in Judea and Samaria, whether committed by Palestinians or Israelis. We take this incident seriously and act against those responsible. But the obstacle to peace has never been those Israeli communities. The fundamental challenge is the absence of a partner committing to peace. Should I remain this council of Hamas's charter that calls for the destruction of Israel and contains apocalyptic calls for violence against Jews, for example, He declares that the day of judgment will not come until Muslims fight and kill Jews. For years, Israeli representatives warned this Council about Hamas and called for its designation as a terrorist organization. Yet some of its members blocked it from even condemning Hamas after the October 7th massacre. Mr. President, last week on the sidelines of High Level Week, We heard calls to protect children in conflict. But nothing was said about Hamas child soldiers, the ones they openly recruit and praise. Recently, Hamas released a video honoring Suhayb Abul Abad, a terrorist who was killed on October 25. The video showed him firing an RPG at Israeli tanks, declaring his loyalty to Hamas, and posing with rifles. He was 16 years old when he died, and even younger when he joined the terror group. He was just one of many minors recruited by Hamas. And the exploitation does not end with recruitment. In a new video released a few days ago by the IDF, a terrorist is seen using a child to move weapons into a civilian home in central Gaza, using the child as a human shield. It is yet another example of the systematic exploitation of children by Hamas to advance attacks against Israeli troops and civilians in violation of international law. I have a copy of this video, which I will share with Council members at the conclusion of today's debate. If this Council is serious about protecting children, it must demand that Hamas stop recruiting children for terrorism. Mr. President, Despite claims made from the General Assembly podium just last week, Hamas operates not only in Gaza, but also in Judea and Samaria. In fact, since 1989, Hamas terrorists from Judea and Samaria have murdered more than 1,000 Israelis and injured over 3,300, from the wave of suicide bombing on Israeli buses, cafes, and other civilian sites in the 1990s and early 2000s, up until today. And behind much of this activity stands Iran. Tehran is responsible for more than half of the funds smuggled into Judea and Samaria to finance Hamas terrorist activity. And it is not just money. Israeli security forces have repeatedly intercepted Iranian weapons bound for Judea and Samaria, including drones, anti-tank rockets, and explosive devices. Iran is training, directing, and arming terrorist groups while providing millions of dollars every month to support their activities in Gaza and Judea and Samaria. Mr. President, Hamas is only part of the terrorist threat Israel faces in Judea and Samaria. The Palestinian Authority, which many see as the basis for a two-state solution, is supposed to prevent terrorism. Instead, it supports it. The Palestinian Authority continues its pay-for-slay policy, payment to terrorists and their families, despite claiming to have ended it. According to a U.S. State Department assessment reported to Congress, more than $150 million was paid in 2025 alone, with payment continuing through alternative channels, including salaries, pensions, and cash. Announcing reform is not the same as delivering it. It must be transparent and verifiable. End payment that reward terrorism, end incitement, and strengthen accountability. Mr. President, in July alone, Israel recorded 331 Palestinian terrorist attacks in Judea and Samaria, including pipe bombs, stabbing, car ramming, arson, and stone throwing. Thankfully, Israel's security forces prevented over 500 more potential attacks. Behind every one of these attacks is a human being whose life can change in an instant. In the past week alone, Israelis faced multiple attacks. Last Wednesday, Neria Leiter, son of Israel's ambassador to the United States, Yechiel Leiter, was seriously injured in a car-ramming attack. He is currently fighting for his life. Ambassador Leiter has already lost another son, Yedidia, fighting Hamas in Gaza in November 2023. Last Sunday, 30-year-old French-Israeli citizen, Netanel Shukun, was shot and murdered in front of his 16-year-old son near a natural spring on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in Judaism. He leaves behind his wife and six children. That wasn't the only attack that Sunday. An Israeli who mistakenly entered a Palestinian village was attacked and injured. Additionally, three separate car-ramming incidents were reported the same day. This is only one day, but it reflects the daily security reality confronting Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria. Mr. President, When this Council debates the obstacles to peace, it must confront the entire picture. Hamas must disarm in Gaza. Hamas and other terrorist organizations must be confronted in Judea and Samaria. Palestinian terrorism must be stopped. And the Palestinian Authority must undertake meaningful reform. Peace cannot be built while terrorism is tolerated, rewarded, or ignored. Thank you.
I thank the representative of Israel for her statement. There are no more names inscribed on the list of speakers. The meeting is adjourned.
